nodes.name: Characteristic graph
nodes.statement: An adequate probabilistic graph $G$ (i.e. a graph with an underlying probability distribution on its vertices) can be associated to a given instance of zero-error source coding problem in Figure \ref{fig:SWzero}, as in Witsenhausen's work \cite{witsenhausen1976zero}. This graph is called ``characteristic graph'' of the problem, as it encompasses the problem data in its structure: the vertices are the source alphabet, with the source probability distribution $P_X$ on these vertices, and two source symbols $xx'$ are adjacent if they are ``confusable'', i.e. $P_{X,Y}(x,y)P_{X,Y}(x',y) > 0$ for some side information symbol $y$.
differentia: the vertices are the source alphabet, with the source probability distribution $P_X$ on these vertices
two source symbols $xx'$ are adjacent if they are ``confusable''
nodes.statement_short: Witsenhausen's characteristic graph: vertices = source symbols with $P_X$, edges join symbols confusable given some side-information value.

nodes.name: Chromatic entropy
nodes.statement_short: Chromatic entropy $H_\chi(G)$: the minimal entropy of a coloring of $G$ (optimal one-shot rate).

nodes.name: Chromatic entropy formula
nodes.statement: H_{\chi}(G)\doteq \inf \lbrace H(c(V)) \:|\: c \text{ is a coloring of } G \rbrace.

nodes.name: Complementary graph entropy (asymptotic optimal rate)
nodes.statement_short: The asymptotic optimal zero-error rate $\overline{H}(G)$ is the normalized limit of chromatic entropies of AND powers of $G$.

nodes.name: Optimal rate as limit of chromatic entropies
nodes.statement: \overline{H}(G) = \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} H_{\chi}(G^{\wedge n}),
nodes.label: eq:debitopti

nodes.name: Optimal rate equals complementary graph entropy
nodes.statement: As shown in \cite{koulgi2003zero}, it is equal to the \emph{complementary graph entropy} defined in \cite{korner1973two}.
conclusions: it is equal to the \emph{complementary graph entropy} defined in \cite{korner1973two}

nodes.name: Pentagon graph $G_5$
nodes.statement: A single-letter formula for $\overline{H}$ is not known, except for perfect graphs \cite{csiszar1990entropy}; and for $G_5 \sqcup G$ and its complement, for all perfect graph $G$ \cite{tuncel2009complementary}, where $G_5$ is the pentagon graph with uniform distribution.
nodes.statement_short: $\overline{H}$ has a single-letter formula only for perfect graphs and $G_5\sqcup G$ ($G$ perfect); $G_5$ is the uniform pentagon.

nodes.statement: Thanks to the side information at the encoder in Figure \ref{fig:Setting}.a, the characteristic graph is the \emph{disjoint union} ($\sqcup$) of a family of auxiliary probabilistic graphs $(G_{z})_{z \in \mathcal{Z}}$; and in Figure \ref{fig:Setting}.b the characteristic graph is the \emph{AND product} ($\wedge$) of the $(G_{z})_{z \in \mathcal{Z}}$.

assumptions: Thanks to the side information at the encoder in Figure \ref{fig:Setting}.a
conclusions: the characteristic graph is the \emph{disjoint union} ($\sqcup$) of a family of auxiliary probabilistic graphs $(G_{z})_{z \in \mathcal{Z}}$

nodes.name: Equality cases of the subadditivity of $\overline{H}$
nodes.statement:
With the subadditivity results in \cite[Theorem 2]{tuncel2009complementary}, we know that $\overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}}^{P_{g(Y)}} G_{z}\big) \leq \sum_{z \in \mathcal{Z}} P_{g(Y)} \overline{H}(G_{z})$ and $\overline{H}\big(\bigwedge_{z \in \mathcal{Z}} G_{z}\big) \leq \sum_{z \in \mathcal{Z}} \overline{H}(G_{z})$ holds in general, 

however characterizing the cases where equality holds is an open problem.
nodes.section: 1.2 Characteristic graph structure in particular instances
nodes.statement_short: Characterize when equality holds in Tuncel et al.'s subadditivity bounds for $\overline{H}$ of disjoint unions and AND products.

nodes.name: Shannon capacity $\Theta$
nodes.statement: Another important problem is the Shannon capacity $\Theta$ of a graph \cite{shannon1956zero}, which characterizes the optimal rate in the zero-error channel coding scenario.

nodes.name: Marton's relation between complementary graph entropy and graph capacity
nodes.statement: Marton has shown in \cite{marton1993shannon} that $\overline{H}(G) + C(G,P) = H(P)$, where $P$ is the underlying probability distribution of $G$, and $C(G,P)$ is the graph capacity relative to $P$.
assumptions: $P$ is the underlying probability distribution of $G$
$C(G,P)$ is the graph capacity relative to $P$

nodes.name: Schrijver's equivalence for Shannon capacity of sums and products
nodes.statement: Recently in \cite{schrijver2023shannon}, Schrijver shows that $\Theta(G \wedge G') = \Theta(G) \Theta(G')$ is equivalent to $\Theta(G \sqcup G') = \Theta(G) + \Theta(G')$.

nodes.name: Sequence notation
nodes.statement: We denote sequences by $x^n = (x_1, ..., x_n)$.

nodes.name: Probability simplex $\Delta(\mathcal{X})$
nodes.statement: The set of probability distributions over $\mathcal{X}$ is denoted by $\Delta(\mathcal{X})$; $P_X \in \Delta(\mathcal{X})$ is the distribution of a random variable $X$.

nodes.name: Uniform distribution
nodes.statement: The uniform distribution is denoted by $\text{Unif}$.

nodes.name: Conditional distribution
nodes.statement: The conditional distribution of $X$ knowing $Y$ is denoted by $P_{X|Y}$.

nodes.name: Probabilistic graph
nodes.statement: A probabilistic graph $G$ is a tuple $(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E}, P_V)$, where $(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E})$ is a graph and $P_V \in \Delta(\mathcal{V})$.

nodes.name: Independent set
nodes.statement: A subset $\mathcal{S} \subseteq \mathcal{V}$ is independent in $G$ if for all $x,x' \in \mathcal{S}$, $xx' \notin \mathcal{E}$.

nodes.name: Coloring
nodes.statement: A mapping $c : \mathcal{V} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}$ is a coloring if $c^{-1}(i)$ is independent for all $i \in \mathcal{C}$.

nodes.name: Cycle, complete and empty graphs
nodes.statement: The cycle, complete, and empty graphs with $n$ vertices are respectively denoted by $C_n$, $K_n$, $N_n$.

nodes.name: AND product $\wedge$
nodes.statement: The AND product of $G_1 = (\mathcal{V}_1, \mathcal{E}_1, P_{V_1})$ and $G_2 = (\mathcal{V}_2, \mathcal{E}_2, P_{V_2})$ is a probabilistic graph denoted by $G_1 \wedge G_2$ with: \begin{itemize}[label = -] \item $\mathcal{V}_1 \times \mathcal{V}_2$ as set of vertices, \item $P_{V_1}P_{V_2}$ as probability distribution on the vertices, \item $(v_1 v_2),(v'_1 v'_2)$ are adjacent if $v_1v'_1 \in \mathcal{E}_1$ AND $v_2v'_2 \in \mathcal{E}_2$; with the convention of self-adjacency for all vertices. \end{itemize} We denote by $G_1^{\wedge n}$ the $n$-th AND power: $G_1^{\wedge n} \doteq G_1 \wedge ... \wedge G_1$.\vspace{-.7em}
nodes.statement_short: AND product of probabilistic graphs: product vertex set and distribution; adjacent iff adjacent (or equal) in every coordinate; $G^{\wedge n}$ its $n$-th power.

nodes.name: Disjoint union $\sqcup$ of probabilistic graphs
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set, and let $P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$. For all $a \in \mathcal{A}$, let $G_a = (\mathcal{V}_a, \mathcal{E}_a, P_{V_a})$ be a probabilistic graph, their disjoint union w.r.t. $P_A$ is a probabilistic graph $(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E}, P_V)$ denoted by $\bigsqcup^{P_A}_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a$ and defined by: \begin{itemize}[label = - ] \item $\mathcal{V} = \bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \mathcal{V}_a$ is the disjoint union of the sets $(\mathcal{V}_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$; \item For all $v,v' \in \mathcal{V}$, $vv' \in \mathcal{E}$ iff they both belong to the same $\mathcal{V}_a$ and $vv' \in \mathcal{E}_a$; \item $P_V = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) P_{V_a}$; note that the $(P_{V_a})_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ have disjoint support in $\mathcal{V}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint union w.r.t. $P_A$: disjoint union of vertex sets and edges, with the mixture distribution $\sum_a P_A(a)P_{V_a}$.
nodes.label: def:disjointunion

nodes.name: Disjoint union vs. union over edges
nodes.statement: The disjoint union $\sqcup$ that we consider here is also called ``sum of graphs'' by Tuncel et al. in \cite{tuncel2009complementary}. Note that $\sqcup$ is the disjoint union over the vertices: it differs in nature from the union over the edges $\cup$ that is already studied in the literature, in particular in \cite{korner1988graphs}, \cite{csiszar1990entropy} and \cite{marton1993shannon}.

nodes.name: Standing notation: $\mathcal{A}$, $P_A$, $(G_a)$
nodes.statement: In this section, $\mathcal{A}$ is a finite set, $P_A$ is a distribution from $\Delta(\mathcal{A})$ and $(G_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ is a family of probabilistic graphs.

nodes.name: Type of a sequence
nodes.statement: Let $a^k \in \mathcal{A}^k$, its type $T_{a^k}$ is its empirical distribution. The set of types of sequences from $\mathcal{A}^k$ is denoted by $\Delta_k(\mathcal{A}) \subset \Delta(\mathcal{A})$.

nodes.name: Complementary graph entropy of a disjoint union w.r.t. a type
nodes.statement: If $P_A \in \Delta_k(\mathcal{A})$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}^\star$ then \begin{equation} \overline{H}\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\right) = \frac{1}{k}\overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge k P_A(a)}\right). \end{equation}
also_stated_at: Theorem \ref{th:partvalues} shows that $\overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big) = \frac{1}{k}\overline{H}\big(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge k P_A(a)}\big)$ holds for all $P_A \in \Delta_k(\mathcal{A})$.
nodes.statement_short: If $P_A$ is a type with denominator $k$, $\overline{H}$ of the disjoint union equals $1/k$ times $\overline{H}$ of an AND product of powers $G_a^{\wedge kP_A(a)}$.
nodes.label: th:partvalues

nodes.name: Disjoint-union / AND-product identity for types
nodes.statement: \overline{H}\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\right) = \frac{1}{k}\overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge k P_A(a)}\right).
nodes.label: eq:corpartvalues

nodes.name: Uniform disjoint union vs. AND product
nodes.statement: $\overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{\mathrm{Unif}(\mathcal{A})} G_a\big) = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{A}|}\overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a\right)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\overline{H}$ of the uniform disjoint union equals $\overline{H}$ of the AND product divided by $|\mathcal{A}|$.
nodes.label: cor:unif

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 1 to a $k$-periodic sequence of type $P_A$ and take every $k$-th term of the limit, which becomes an AND power.

nodes.name: Recall Lemma 1
nodes.statement_short: State the key Lemma 1 expressing $\overline{H}$ of a disjoint union via AND products along a sequence of types.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (complementary graph entropy of a disjoint union as a limit)
nodes.statement: Let $(\overline{a}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star} \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{N}^\star}$ be any sequence such that $T_{\overline{a}^n} \rightarrow P_A$ when $n \rightarrow \infty$. Then we have \begin{equation} \overline{H}\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \right) = \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n}H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n} (a)}\right). \end{equation}
assumptions: $(\overline{a}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star} \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{N}^\star}$ be any sequence such that $T_{\overline{a}^n} \rightarrow P_A$ when $n \rightarrow \infty$
nodes.statement_short: For any sequence whose types converge to $P_A$, $\overline{H}$ of the disjoint union is the limit of normalized chromatic entropies of AND products of powers.
nodes.label: lemma:partvalues

nodes.name: Lemma 1 limit formula
nodes.statement: \overline{H}\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \right) = \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n}H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n} (a)}\right).
nodes.label: eq:lemmapartvaluesA

nodes.name: Choose a $k$-periodic sequence
nodes.statement: Now let us prove Theorem \ref{th:partvalues}. Let $(\overline{a}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star}$ be a $k$-periodic sequence such that $T_{\overline{a}^k} = P_A$, then $T_{\overline{a}^{nk}} = T_{\overline{a}^k}$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}^\star$, and $T_{\overline{a}^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} P_A$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a $k$-periodic sequence of type $P_A$, so its types converge to $P_A$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 1 on every $k$-th term
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 1 along the subsequence $kn$ and recognize an AND power, giving $\frac1k\overline{H}$.

nodes.name: Induced subgraph
nodes.statement: The subgraph induced in a graph $G$ by a subset of vertices $\mathcal{S}$ is the graph obtained from $G$ by keeping only the vertices in $\mathcal{S}$ and the edges between them, and is denoted by $G[\mathcal{S}]$. When $G$ is a probabilistic graph, we give it the underlying probability distribution $P_V/P_V(\mathcal{S})$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Single-letter formula of $\overline{H}$ for products of perfect graphs

nodes.name: Perfect graph
nodes.statement: A graph $G = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E})$ is perfect if $\:\forall \mathcal{S} \subset \mathcal{V}, \; \chi(G[\mathcal{S}]) = \omega(G[\mathcal{S}])$; where $\omega$ is the size of the largest clique (i.e. complete induced subgraph); and $\chi(G[\mathcal{S}])$ is the smallest $|\mathcal{C}|$ such that there exists a coloring $c : \mathcal{S} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}$ of $G[\mathcal{S}]$. By extension, we call perfect a probabilistic graph $(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E}, P_{V})$ if $(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E})$ is perfect.
nodes.section: 4.1 Single-letter formula of $\overline{H}$ for products of perfect graphs
nodes.statement_short: A graph is perfect if every induced subgraph has chromatic number equal to clique number; extended to probabilistic graphs.

nodes.name: Körner graph entropy $H_\kappa$
nodes.statement: For all $G = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E}, P_V)$, let $\Gamma(G)$ be the collection of independent sets of vertices in $G$. The K\"{o}rner graph entropy of $G$ is defined by \begin{align} H_\kappa(G) = \min_{V \in W \in \Gamma(G)} I(W;V), \end{align} where the minimum is taken over all distributions $P_{W|V} \in \Delta(\mathcal{W})^{\mathcal{V}}$, with $\mathcal{W} = \Gamma(G)$ and with the constraint that the random vertex $V$ belongs to the random independent set $W$ with probability one, i.e. $V \in W \in \Gamma(G)$ in \eqref{eq:wheee}.
nodes.section: 4.1 Single-letter formula of $\overline{H}$ for products of perfect graphs
nodes.statement_short: Körner graph entropy: minimal mutual information $I(W;V)$ over random independent sets $W$ containing the random vertex $V$.

nodes.name: Körner graph entropy formula
nodes.statement: H_\kappa(G) = \min_{V \in W \in \Gamma(G)} I(W;V),
nodes.section: 4.1 Single-letter formula of $\overline{H}$ for products of perfect graphs
nodes.label: eq:wheee

nodes.name: Strong perfect graph theorem
nodes.statement: A graph $G$ is perfect if and only if neither $G$ nor its complement have an induced odd cycle of length at least 5.
nodes.section: 4.1 Single-letter formula of $\overline{H}$ for products of perfect graphs
conclusions: A graph $G$ is perfect if and only if neither $G$ nor its complement have an induced odd cycle of length at least 5.
equivalent_conditions: neither $G$ nor its complement have an induced odd cycle of length at least 5
nodes.label: th:strongperfect

nodes.name: Complementary graph entropy of perfect graphs equals Körner entropy
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a perfect probabilistic graph, then $\overline{H}(G) = H_\kappa(G)$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Single-letter formula of $\overline{H}$ for products of perfect graphs
nodes.label: th:Hbarperfect

nodes.name: Single-letter formula of $\overline{H}$ for products of perfect graphs
nodes.statement: When $(G_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ is a family of perfect probabilistic graphs, the following single-letter characterizations hold: \begin{align} & \overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a \right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \overline{H}(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} H_\kappa(G_a), \\ & \overline{H}\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \overline{H}(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) H_\kappa(G_a). \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.1 Single-letter formula of $\overline{H}$ for products of perfect graphs
assumptions: $(G_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ is a family of perfect probabilistic graphs
conclusions: & \overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a \right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \overline{H}(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} H_\kappa(G_a), \\ & \overline{H}\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \overline{H}(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) H_\kappa(G_a).
nodes.statement_short: For perfect $G_a$, $\overline{H}$ of their AND product is the sum, and of their disjoint union the $P_A$-average, of the Körner entropies.
nodes.label: th:mainperfect

nodes.statement: & \overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a \right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \overline{H}(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} H_\kappa(G_a), \\ & \overline{H}\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \overline{H}(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) H_\kappa(G_a).

nodes.name: Subadditivity of complementary graph entropy (Tuncel et al.)
nodes.statement: & \overline{H}(G_1 \overset{(\alpha, 1-\alpha)}{\sqcup} G_2) \leq \alpha \overline{H}(G_1) + (1-\alpha)\overline{H}(G_2), \\ & \overline{H}(G_1 \wedge G_2) \leq \overline{H}(G_1) + \overline{H}(G_2).
nodes.section: 4.2 Linearization of the complementary graph entropy
nodes.statement_short: $\overline{H}$ is subadditive under disjoint union (convex combination bound) and AND product (sum bound).
nodes.label: eq:tuncelA

nodes.name: Linearization equivalence for two graphs
nodes.statement: For all probabilistic graphs $G_1, G_2$, for all $\alpha \in (0,1)$, we have: \begin{align} & \overline{H}(G_1 \overset{(\alpha, 1-\alpha)}{\sqcup} G_2) = \alpha \overline{H}(G_1) + (1-\alpha)\overline{H}(G_2) \\ \Longleftrightarrow\: & \overline{H}(G_1 \wedge G_2) = \overline{H}(G_1) + \overline{H}(G_2). \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.2 Linearization of the complementary graph entropy
assumptions: For all probabilistic graphs $G_1, G_2$, for all $\alpha \in (0,1)$
nodes.statement_short: Equality in Tuncel et al.'s disjoint-union bound holds iff equality holds in the AND-product bound.
nodes.label: th:caraclinspec

nodes.name: Two-graph linearization equivalence
nodes.statement: & \overline{H}(G_1 \overset{(\alpha, 1-\alpha)}{\sqcup} G_2) = \alpha \overline{H}(G_1) + (1-\alpha)\overline{H}(G_2) \\ \Longleftrightarrow\: & \overline{H}(G_1 \wedge G_2) = \overline{H}(G_1) + \overline{H}(G_2).
nodes.section: 4.2 Linearization of the complementary graph entropy

nodes.name: Linearization equivalence for families of graphs
nodes.statement: Let $P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$ with full-support, then the following equivalence holds \begin{align} & \overline{H}\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \overline{H}(G_a) \\ \Longleftrightarrow \;\; & \overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a\right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \overline{H}(G_a). \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.2 Linearization of the complementary graph entropy
nodes.statement_short: For full-support $P_A$, $\overline{H}$ of the disjoint union is linear in the $\overline{H}(G_a)$ iff $\overline{H}$ of the AND product is additive.
nodes.label: th:caraclin

nodes.name: Family linearization equivalence
nodes.statement: & \overline{H}\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \overline{H}(G_a) \\ \Longleftrightarrow \;\; & \overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a\right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \overline{H}(G_a).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to typical type classes (Lemma 3), distribute $\wedge$ over $\sqcup$ (Lemma 2) and sandwich the chromatic entropy between AND products whose exponents differ by $\lceil 2n\epsilon\rceil$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2 (distributivity of $\wedge$ w.r.t. $\sqcup$)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}$ be finite sets, let $P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$ and $P_B \in \Delta(\mathcal{B})$. For all $a \in \mathcal{A}$ and $b \in \mathcal{B}$, let $G_a = (\mathcal{V}_a, \mathcal{E}_a, P_{V_a})$ and $G_b = (\mathcal{V}_b, \mathcal{E}_b, P_{V_b})$ be probabilistic graphs. Then \begin{align} \left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\right) \wedge \left(\bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}}^{P_B} G_b\right) = \bigsqcup_{(a,b) \in \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}}^{P_AP_B} G_a \wedge G_b. \end{align}
assumptions: $G_a = (\mathcal{V}_a, \mathcal{E}_a, P_{V_a})$ and $G_b = (\mathcal{V}_b, \mathcal{E}_b, P_{V_b})$ be probabilistic graphs
nodes.statement_short: The AND product of two disjoint unions is the disjoint union, w.r.t. the product distribution, of the pairwise AND products.
nodes.label: lemma:distrib

nodes.name: Distributivity identity
nodes.statement: \left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\right) \wedge \left(\bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}}^{P_B} G_b\right) = \bigsqcup_{(a,b) \in \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}}^{P_AP_B} G_a \wedge G_b.
nodes.label: eq:distribunion

nodes.name: Lemma 3 (complementary graph entropy via high-probability induced subgraphs)
nodes.statement: Let $G = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E}, P_V)$, and $(\mathcal{S}^n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star}$ be a sequence of sets such that for all $n \in \mathbb{N}^\star$, $\mathcal{S}^n \subset \mathcal{V}^n$, and $P^n_V(\mathcal{S}^n) \rightarrow 1$ when $n \rightarrow \infty$. Then $\overline{H}(G) = \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} H_\chi\big(G^{\wedge n}[\mathcal{S}^n]\big)$.
assumptions: $(\mathcal{S}^n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star}$ be a sequence of sets such that for all $n \in \mathbb{N}^\star$, $\mathcal{S}^n \subset \mathcal{V}^n$, and $P^n_V(\mathcal{S}^n) \rightarrow 1$ when $n \rightarrow \infty$
nodes.statement_short: $\overline{H}$ can be computed from subgraphs of AND powers induced by vertex sets of asymptotic probability one.
nodes.label: lemma:simplificationinduced

nodes.name: Isomorphic probabilistic graphs
nodes.statement: Let $G_1 = (\mathcal{V}_1, \mathcal{E}_1, P_{V_1})$ and $G_2 = (\mathcal{V}_2, \mathcal{E}_2, P_{V_2})$. We say that $G_1$ is isomorphic to $G_2$ if there exists an isomorphism between them, i.e. a bijection $\psi : \mathcal{V}_1 \rightarrow \mathcal{V}_2$ such that: \begin{itemize}[label = - ] \item For all $v_1, v_1' \in \mathcal{V}_1$, $v_1 v'_1 \in \mathcal{E}_1 \Longleftrightarrow \psi(v_1)\psi(v'_1) \in \mathcal{E}_2$, \item For all $v_1 \in \mathcal{V}_1$, $P_{V_1}(v_1) = P_{V_2}\big(\psi(v_1)\big)$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Two probabilistic graphs are isomorphic if a bijection preserves both adjacency and vertex probabilities.

nodes.name: Lemma 4 (chromatic entropy of a disjoint union of isomorphic graphs)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a finite set, let $P_B \in \Delta(\mathcal{B})$ and let $(G_b)_{b \in \mathcal{B}}$ be a family of isomorphic probabilistic graphs, then $H_\chi\big(\bigsqcup_{b' \in \mathcal{B}}^{P_B} G_{b'} \big) = H_\chi(G_b)$ for all $b \in \mathcal{B}$.
assumptions: $(G_b)_{b \in \mathcal{B}}$ be a family of isomorphic probabilistic graphs
nodes.label: lemma:unionisomorph

nodes.name: Set up graphs and sequence
nodes.statement: For all $a \in \mathcal{A}$, let $G_a = (\mathcal{V}_a, \mathcal{E}_a, P_{V_A})$, and let $G = \bigsqcup^{P_A}_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a$. Let $P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$, and let $(\overline{a}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star} \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{N}^\star}$ be a sequence such that $T_{\overline{a}^n} \rightarrow P_A$ when $n \rightarrow \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the graphs, their disjoint union $G$ and a sequence with types converging to $P_A$.

nodes.name: Define typical types and sets
nodes.statement_short: Define the $\epsilon$-typical type class, the normalized distribution $P'^n$ and the typical vertex set $\mathcal{S}^n_\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Restrict to typical set via Lemma 3
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3 reduces $\overline{H}(G)$ to AND powers restricted to the typical set.

nodes.name: Typical type class and typical vertex set
nodes.statement: & \mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A) \doteq \big\lbrace a^n \in \mathcal{A}^n \:\big|\: \| T_{a^n} - P_A \|_\infty \leq \epsilon \big\rbrace, \\ & P'^n \doteq \frac{P^n_A}{P^n_A(\mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A))},\qquad \mathcal{S}_\epsilon^n \doteq \bigsqcup_{a^n \in \mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A)} \;\prod_{t \leq n} \mathcal{V}_{a_t}. \nonumber
nodes.label: eq:lemmapartA0

nodes.name: Restriction to the typical set
nodes.statement: \overline{H}(G) = \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n}H_\chi\Big(G^{\wedge n}[\mathcal{S}^n_\epsilon]\Big),
nodes.label: eq:conclemmapart1

nodes.name: Compare types
nodes.statement_short: For large $n$ the reference sequence is typical, so all typical types are within $2\epsilon$ of its type.

nodes.name: Type closeness bound
nodes.statement: \big|T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')-T_{a^n}(a')\big|\leq 2\epsilon.
nodes.label: eq:lemmapartB0

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement:
We have on one hand
\begin{align}
    & H_\chi\Big(\big(\textstyle\bigsqcup^{P_A}_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a\big)^{\wedge n}[\mathcal{S}^n_\epsilon]\Big) \nonumber\\
    =  \; & H_\chi\left(\left(\textstyle\bigsqcup_{a^n \in \mathcal{A}^n}^{P_A^n} \; \textstyle\bigwedge_{t \leq n} G_{a_t}\right)[\mathcal{S}^n_\epsilon]\right) \\
    = \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigsqcup_{a^n \in \mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A)}^{P'^n} \;\textstyle\bigwedge_{t \leq n} G_{a_t}\right) \\
    = \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigsqcup_{a^n \in \mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A)}^{P'^n} \; \textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{a^n}(a')}\right) \\
    \leq \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigsqcup_{a^n \in \mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A)}^{P'^n} \; \textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a') + \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil}\right) \\
    = \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a') + \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil}\right) \\
    \leq \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')}\right) + H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge \lceil 2 n\epsilon\rceil}\right) \\
    \leq \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')}\right) + \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil|\mathcal{A}|\log|\mathcal{V}|; \end{align}
where \eqref{eq:lemmapartB1} comes from Lemma \ref{lemma:distrib}; \eqref{eq:lemmapartB2} comes from the definition of $\mathcal{S}_\epsilon^n$ and $P'^n$ in \eqref{eq:lemmapartA0}; \eqref{eq:lemmapartB3} is a rearrangement of the terms inside the product; \eqref{eq:lemmapartB4} comes from \eqref{eq:lemmapartB0}; \eqref{eq:lemmapartB5} follows from Lemma \ref{lemma:unionisomorph}, the graphs $\big(\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a') + \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil}\big)_{a^n \in \mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A)}$ are isomorphic as they do not depend on $a^n$; \eqref{eq:lemmapartB5a} follows from the subadditivity of $H_\chi$; and \eqref{eq:lemmapartB6} is the upper bound on $H_\chi$ given by the highest entropy of a coloring.
nodes.statement_short: Upper-bound the chromatic entropy on the typical set by an AND product with exponents raised by $\lceil 2n\epsilon\rceil$ (Lemmas 2 and 4, subadditivity).

nodes.name: Upper bound chain
nodes.statement: & H_\chi\Big(\big(\textstyle\bigsqcup^{P_A}_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a\big)^{\wedge n}[\mathcal{S}^n_\epsilon]\Big) \nonumber\\ = \; & H_\chi\left(\left(\textstyle\bigsqcup_{a^n \in \mathcal{A}^n}^{P_A^n} \; \textstyle\bigwedge_{t \leq n} G_{a_t}\right)[\mathcal{S}^n_\epsilon]\right) \\ = \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigsqcup_{a^n \in \mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A)}^{P'^n} \;\textstyle\bigwedge_{t \leq n} G_{a_t}\right) \\ = \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigsqcup_{a^n \in \mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A)}^{P'^n} \; \textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{a^n}(a')}\right) \\ \leq \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigsqcup_{a^n \in \mathcal{T}^n_\epsilon(P_A)}^{P'^n} \; \textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a') + \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil}\right) \\ = \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a') + \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil}\right) \\ \leq \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')}\right) + H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge \lceil 2 n\epsilon\rceil}\right) \\ \leq \; & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')}\right) + \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil|\mathcal{A}|\log|\mathcal{V}|;
nodes.label: eq:lemmapartB1

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, we obtain with similar arguments
\begin{align}
    & H_\chi\Big(\big(\textstyle\bigsqcup^{P_A}_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a\big)^{\wedge n}[\mathcal{S}^n_\epsilon]\Big) \nonumber\\
    \geq \: & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a') - \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil}\right) \\
    \geq \: & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')}\right) - H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge \lceil 2 n\epsilon\rceil}\right), \\
    \geq \: & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')}\right) - \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil|\mathcal{A}|\log|\mathcal{V}|. \end{align}
Note that \eqref{eq:lemmapartC4a} also comes from the subadditivity of $H_\chi$ : $H_\chi(G_2) \geq H_\chi(G_1 \wedge G_2) - H_\chi(G_1)$ for all $G_1, G_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric lower bound with exponents lowered by $\lceil 2n\epsilon\rceil$.

nodes.name: Lower bound chain
nodes.statement: & H_\chi\Big(\big(\textstyle\bigsqcup^{P_A}_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a\big)^{\wedge n}[\mathcal{S}^n_\epsilon]\Big) \nonumber\\ \geq \: & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a') - \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil}\right)\\ \geq \: & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')}\right) - H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge \lceil 2 n\epsilon\rceil}\right),\\ \geq \: & H_\chi\left(\textstyle\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')}\right) - \lceil 2 n\epsilon \rceil|\mathcal{A}|\log|\mathcal{V}|.
nodes.label: eq:lemmapartC3

nodes.name: Combine bounds
nodes.statement_short: The two limits differ by at most $2\epsilon|\mathcal{A}|\log|\mathcal{V}|$.

nodes.name: Limits differ by $O(\epsilon)$
nodes.statement: & \left|\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} H_\chi(G^{\wedge n}[\mathcal{S}^n_\epsilon]) - \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} G_{a'}^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n}(a')}\right)\right| \nonumber \\ & \leq 2\epsilon|\mathcal{A}|\log|\mathcal{V}|.
nodes.label: eq:conclemmapart2

nodes.name: Let epsilon vanish
nodes.statement: As this holds for all $\epsilon > 0$, combining \eqref{eq:conclemmapart1} and \eqref{eq:conclemmapart2} yields the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Let $\epsilon\to0$ to conclude.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.8
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 3.3 links the uniform disjoint union to the AND product; convexity of $P_A\mapsto\overline{H}(\sqcup^{P_A})$ (Lemma 5) and Lemma 6 turn equality at one interior point into linearity.

nodes.name: Lemma 5 (convexity and Lipschitz continuity of $P_A \mapsto \overline{H}(\sqcup^{P_A} G_a)$)
nodes.statement: The function $P_A \mapsto \overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big)$ is convex and $(\log \max_a |\mathcal{V}_a|)$-Lipschitz.
conclusions: The function $P_A \mapsto \overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big)$ is convex and $(\log \max_a |\mathcal{V}_a|)$-Lipschitz.
nodes.statement_short: $P_A\mapsto\overline{H}$ of the disjoint union is convex and $\log\max_a|\mathcal{V}_a|$-Lipschitz.
nodes.label: th:etaconvex

nodes.name: Lemma 6 (convex function meeting linear interpolation at an interior point is linear)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set, and $\gamma : \Delta(\mathcal{A}) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a convex function. Then the following holds: \begin{align} & \exists P_A \in \mathrm{int}(\Delta(\mathcal{A})), \, \gamma(P_A) = \textstyle\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \gamma(\mathds{1}_a) \\ \Longleftrightarrow \;\; & \forall P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A}), \, \gamma(P_A) = \textstyle\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \gamma(\mathds{1}_a) \end{align} where $\mathrm{int}(\Delta(\mathcal{A}))$ is the interior of $\Delta(\mathcal{A})$ (i.e. the full-support distributions on $\mathcal{A}$).
nodes.statement_short: A convex function on the simplex equals its vertex interpolation at some interior point iff it does so everywhere.
nodes.label: lemma:convexanalysis

nodes.name: Interior-point vs. global linearity
nodes.statement: & \exists P_A \in \mathrm{int}(\Delta(\mathcal{A})), \, \gamma(P_A) = \textstyle\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \gamma(\mathds{1}_a) \\ \Longleftrightarrow \;\; & \forall P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A}), \, \gamma(P_A) = \textstyle\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \gamma(\mathds{1}_a)
nodes.label: eq:lemma1A

nodes.name: Forward direction
nodes.statement_short: Additivity of the AND product gives equality at the uniform interior point (Cor. 3.3); convexity and Lemma 6 give linearity everywhere.

nodes.name: Linearity of $\overline{H}$ of disjoint unions
nodes.statement: \forall P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A}),\; \overline{H}\big(\textstyle\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big) = \textstyle\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \overline{H}(G_a).
nodes.label: eq:proofcormainB

nodes.name: Converse direction
nodes.statement: $(\Longleftarrow)$ Conversely, assume \eqref{eq:proofcormainB}, then $P_A \mapsto \overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big)$ is linear. We can use Corollary \ref{cor:unif}, and we have $\overline{H}\big( \bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a \big) = |\mathcal{A}|\overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{\mathrm{Unif}(\mathcal{A})} G_a\big) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \overline{H}(G_{a})$.
nodes.statement_short: Linearity at the uniform distribution plus Corollary 3.3 gives additivity of the AND product.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6
nodes.statement:
For all $a \in \mathcal{A}$, let $G_a = (\mathcal{V}_a, \mathcal{E}_a, P_{V_a})$ be a perfect probabilistic graph. By Lemma \ref{lemma:perfectunion}, $\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a$ is also perfect; and we have $\overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big) = H_\kappa\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big)$ by Theorem \ref{th:Hbarperfect}. We also have $H_\kappa\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) H_\kappa(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \overline{H}(G_a)$ by Lemma \ref{lemma:Hkappasplit} and Theorem \ref{th:Hbarperfect} used on the perfect graphs $(G_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$.

Therefore \eqref{eq:cormain01a} is satisfied by the graphs $(G_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $P_A$: by Theorem \ref{th:caraclin}, it follows that $\overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a \right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \overline{H}(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} H_\kappa(G_a)$, where the last equality comes from Theorem \ref{th:Hbarperfect}.
nodes.statement_short: The disjoint union of perfect graphs is perfect (Lemma 8), so its $\overline{H}$ is a Körner entropy, which splits linearly (Lemma 7); Theorem 4.8 transfers this to the AND product.

nodes.name: Lemma 7 (Körner graph entropy of a disjoint union)
nodes.statement: For all probabilistic graphs $(G_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$, we have $H_\kappa\big(\bigsqcup_{a\in\mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \big) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) H_\kappa(G_a)$.
nodes.label: lemma:Hkappasplit

nodes.name: Lemma 8 (disjoint union of perfect graphs)
nodes.statement: The probabilistic graph $\bigsqcup_{a\in\mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a$ is perfect if and only if $G_a$ is perfect for all $a \in \mathcal{A}$.
conclusions: The probabilistic graph $\bigsqcup_{a\in\mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a$ is perfect if and only if  $G_a$ is perfect for all $a \in \mathcal{A}$.
equivalent_conditions: The probabilistic graph $\bigsqcup_{a\in\mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a$ is perfect
nodes.label: lemma:perfectunion

nodes.name: Disjoint union is perfect
nodes.statement: For all $a \in \mathcal{A}$, let $G_a = (\mathcal{V}_a, \mathcal{E}_a, P_{V_a})$ be a perfect probabilistic graph. By Lemma \ref{lemma:perfectunion}, $\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a$ is also perfect; and we have $\overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big) = H_\kappa\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big)$ by Theorem \ref{th:Hbarperfect}.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 8 the disjoint union is perfect, so its $\overline{H}$ equals its Körner entropy.

nodes.name: Split the Körner entropy
nodes.statement: We also have $H_\kappa\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) H_\kappa(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \overline{H}(G_a)$ by Lemma \ref{lemma:Hkappasplit} and Theorem \ref{th:Hbarperfect} used on the perfect graphs $(G_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7 and Theorem 4.5 give the $P_A$-average formula.

nodes.name: Transfer to the AND product
nodes.statement: Therefore \eqref{eq:cormain01a} is satisfied by the graphs $(G_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $P_A$: by Theorem \ref{th:caraclin}, it follows that $\overline{H}\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a \right) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \overline{H}(G_a) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} H_\kappa(G_a)$, where the last equality comes from Theorem \ref{th:Hbarperfect}.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 4.8 turns the linear disjoint-union formula into additivity for the AND product.

nodes.name: Optimal rates of the two particular settings
nodes.statement: The optimal rates in the settings from Figure \ref{fig:Setting}.a and Figure \ref{fig:Setting}.b are respectively given by $\overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}}^{P_{g(Y)}} G_{z}\big)$ and $\overline{H}\big(\bigwedge_{z \in \mathcal{Z}} G_{z}\big)$.
conclusions: The optimal rates in the settings from Figure \ref{fig:Setting}.a and Figure \ref{fig:Setting}.b are respectively given by $\overline{H}\big(\bigsqcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}}^{P_{g(Y)}} G_{z}\big)$ and $\overline{H}\big(\bigwedge_{z \in \mathcal{Z}} G_{z}\big)$.
nodes.statement_short: The optimal zero-error rates of the two settings are $\overline{H}$ of the disjoint union and of the AND product of the auxiliary graphs.
nodes.label: prop:optimalrate

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4.9
nodes.statement_short: Tuncel et al.'s Lemma 3 gives linearity of the disjoint union of $G$ and $G_5$; Theorem 4.8 transfers it to $G\wedge G_5$, with $\overline{H}(G_5)=\frac12\log5$.

nodes.name: Linearity for $G \sqcup G_5$
nodes.statement: \overline{H}(G \overset{(\alpha, 1-\alpha)}{\sqcup} G_5) = \alpha \overline{H}(G) + (1-\alpha)\overline{H}(G_5).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement_short: Check that both sides have the same vertex set and distribution, then that adjacency coincides via a chain of equivalences.

nodes.name: Same vertices and distribution
nodes.statement_short: Both sides have the same vertex set and the same product distribution.

nodes.name: Common vertex set
nodes.statement: \left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \mathcal{V}_a\right) \times \left(\bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \mathcal{V}_b\right) = \bigsqcup_{(a,b) \in \mathcal{A}\times \mathcal{B}} \mathcal{V}_a \times \mathcal{V}_b

nodes.name: Common distribution
nodes.statement: & \left(\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) P_{V_a}\right)\left(\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} P_B(b) P_{V_b}\right) \nonumber\\ & = \sum_{(a,b) \in \mathcal{A}\times \mathcal{B}} P_A(a) P_B(b) P_{V_a} P_{V_b}.

nodes.name: Same edges
nodes.statement:
Now let us show that these two graphs have the same edges. Let $(v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \in \left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \mathcal{V}_a\right) \times \left(\bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \mathcal{V}_b\right)$; let $a_*, a'_* \in \mathcal{A}$ and $b_*,b'_* \in \mathcal{B}$ be the unique indexes such that
    \begin{align}
        (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}) \in \mathcal{V}_{a_*} \times \mathcal{V}_{b_*} \quad \text{and} \quad (v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \in \mathcal{V}_{a'_*} \times \mathcal{V}_{b'_*}.
    \end{align}
    We have:
    \begin{align}
        &  \!\!\! (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \text{ are adjacent in } \left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\right) \wedge \left(\bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}}^{P_B} G_b\right)\\
        \Longleftrightarrow & \; v_{\mathcal{A}}, v'_{\mathcal{A}} \text{ adjacent in } \bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \text{ and } \nonumber\\
        & v_{\mathcal{B}}, v'_{\mathcal{B}} \text{ adjacent in } \bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}}^{P_B} G_b\\
        \Longleftrightarrow & \; a_* = a'_* \text{ and } v_{\mathcal{A}} v'_{\mathcal{A}} \in \mathcal{E}_{a_*} \text{ and } b_* = b'_* \text{ and } v_{\mathcal{B}} v'_{\mathcal{B}} \in \mathcal{E}_{b_*} \\
        \Longleftrightarrow & \; (a_*,b_*) = (a'_*, b'_*) \text{ and } \nonumber\\ 
        & \; (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \text{ are adjacent in } G_{a_*} \wedge G_{b_*} \\
        \Longleftrightarrow & \; (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \text{ are adjacent in } \bigsqcup_{(a,b) \in \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}}^{P_AP_B} G_a \wedge G_b.
    \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Show adjacency coincides in both graphs.

nodes.name: Locate the components
nodes.statement_short: Take two vertices and the unique component indices containing them.

nodes.name: Component indices
nodes.statement: (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}) \in \mathcal{V}_{a_*} \times \mathcal{V}_{b_*} \quad \text{and} \quad (v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \in \mathcal{V}_{a'_*} \times \mathcal{V}_{b'_*}.

nodes.name: Chain of adjacency equivalences
nodes.statement:
We have:
    \begin{align}
        &  \!\!\! (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \text{ are adjacent in } \left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\right) \wedge \left(\bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}}^{P_B} G_b\right)\\
        \Longleftrightarrow & \; v_{\mathcal{A}}, v'_{\mathcal{A}} \text{ adjacent in } \bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \text{ and } \nonumber\\
        & v_{\mathcal{B}}, v'_{\mathcal{B}} \text{ adjacent in } \bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}}^{P_B} G_b\\
        \Longleftrightarrow & \; a_* = a'_* \text{ and } v_{\mathcal{A}} v'_{\mathcal{A}} \in \mathcal{E}_{a_*} \text{ and } b_* = b'_* \text{ and } v_{\mathcal{B}} v'_{\mathcal{B}} \in \mathcal{E}_{b_*} \\
        \Longleftrightarrow & \; (a_*,b_*) = (a'_*, b'_*) \text{ and } \nonumber\\ 
        & \; (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \text{ are adjacent in } G_{a_*} \wedge G_{b_*} \\
        \Longleftrightarrow & \; (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \text{ are adjacent in } \bigsqcup_{(a,b) \in \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}}^{P_AP_B} G_a \wedge G_b.
    \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the definitions of $\wedge$ and $\sqcup$ to show the adjacency relations are equivalent.

nodes.name: Adjacency equivalence chain
nodes.statement: & \!\!\! (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \text{ are adjacent in } \left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\right) \wedge \left(\bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}}^{P_B} G_b\right)\\ \Longleftrightarrow & \; v_{\mathcal{A}}, v'_{\mathcal{A}} \text{ adjacent in } \bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \text{ and } \nonumber\\ & v_{\mathcal{B}}, v'_{\mathcal{B}} \text{ adjacent in } \bigsqcup_{b \in \mathcal{B}}^{P_B} G_b\\ \Longleftrightarrow & \; a_* = a'_* \text{ and } v_{\mathcal{A}} v'_{\mathcal{A}} \in \mathcal{E}_{a_*} \text{ and } b_* = b'_* \text{ and } v_{\mathcal{B}} v'_{\mathcal{B}} \in \mathcal{E}_{b_*} \\ \Longleftrightarrow & \; (a_*,b_*) = (a'_*, b'_*) \text{ and } \nonumber\\ & \; (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \text{ are adjacent in } G_{a_*} \wedge G_{b_*} \\ \Longleftrightarrow & \; (v_{\mathcal{A}},v_{\mathcal{B}}),(v'_{\mathcal{A}},v'_{\mathcal{B}}) \text{ are adjacent in } \bigsqcup_{(a,b) \in \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}}^{P_AP_B} G_a \wedge G_b.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement_short: Sandwich the chromatic entropy of the induced subgraph of $G^{\wedge n}$ using Lemma 9, then normalize by $n$ and take the limit.

nodes.name: Lemma 9 (chromatic entropy of an induced subgraph)
nodes.statement: Let $G = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E}, P_V)$ and $\mathcal{S} \subset \mathcal{V}$, then \begin{align} H_\chi(G) - 1 - (1-P_V(\mathcal{S}))\log|\mathcal{V}| \leq H_\chi(G[\mathcal{S}]) \leq\frac{H_\chi(G)}{P_V(\mathcal{S})}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $H_\chi(G[\mathcal{S}])$ is between $H_\chi(G)-1-(1-P_V(\mathcal{S}))\log|\mathcal{V}|$ and $H_\chi(G)/P_V(\mathcal{S})$.
nodes.label: lemma:induced

nodes.name: Induced-subgraph chromatic entropy bounds
nodes.statement: H_\chi(G) - 1 - (1-P_V(\mathcal{S}))\log|\mathcal{V}| \leq H_\chi(G[\mathcal{S}]) \leq\frac{H_\chi(G)}{P_V(\mathcal{S})}.

nodes.name: Induced subgraph can have larger chromatic entropy
nodes.statement: $H_\chi(G[\mathcal{S}])$ can be greater than $H_\chi(G)$, even if $G[\mathcal{S}]$ has less vertices and inherits the structure of $G$. This stems from the normalized distribution $P_V/P_V(\mathcal{S})$ on the vertices of $G[\mathcal{S}]$ which gives more weight to the vertices in $\mathcal{S}$. For example, consider \begin{align} G = \big(N_5, \mathrm{Unif}(\lbrace 1, ..., 5\rbrace)\big) \overset{(1-\epsilon,\epsilon)}{\sqcup} \big(K_5, \mathrm{Unif}(\lbrace 1, ..., 5\rbrace)\big),\nonumber \end{align} with $\mathcal{S}$ being the vertices in the connected component $K_5$ in $G$. Then $H_\chi(G) = \epsilon \log 5$ and $H_\chi(G[\mathcal{S}]) = \log 5$.
nodes.statement_short: Because of renormalization, $H_\chi(G[\mathcal{S}])$ can exceed $H_\chi(G)$, e.g. $\epsilon\log5$ vs. $\log5$ for an empty/complete union.

nodes.name: Bounds for AND powers
nodes.statement: & H_\chi(G^{\wedge n}) - 1 - (1-P^n_V(\mathcal{S}^n))\log|\mathcal{V}| \nonumber\\ \leq \: & H_\chi(G^{\wedge n}[\mathcal{S}^n]) \leq \frac{H_\chi(G^{\wedge n})}{P^n_V(\mathcal{S}^n)}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement_short: Via Lemma 1, compare chromatic entropies of AND products along type sequences: subadditivity gives the Lipschitz bound, and type splitting (Lemma 10) gives convexity.

nodes.name: Type-splitting lemma
nodes.statement: Let $(\overline{a}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star} \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{N}^\star}$ be a sequence such that $T_{\overline{a}^n} \rightarrow P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$ when $n \rightarrow \infty$, let $\beta \in (0,1)$ and $P'_A, P''_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$ such that \begin{align} P_A = \beta P'_A + (1-\beta)P''_A. \end{align} Then there exists a sequence $(b_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star} \in \lbrace 0, 1 \rbrace^{\mathbb{N}^\star}$ such that the two extracted sequences $a' \doteq (\overline{a}_n)_{\substack{n\in \mathbb{N}^\star, \\ b_n = 0}}$ and $a'' \doteq (\overline{a}_n)_{\substack{n\in \mathbb{N}^\star, \\ b_n = 1}}$ satisfy \begin{align} & T_{b^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} (\beta, 1-\beta), & & \\ & T_{a'^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} P'_A, & & T_{a''^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} P''_A. \end{align}
assumptions: $(\overline{a}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star} \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{N}^\star}$ be a sequence such that $T_{\overline{a}^n} \rightarrow P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$ when $n \rightarrow \infty$
conclusions: there exists a sequence $(b_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}^\star} \in \lbrace 0, 1 \rbrace^{\mathbb{N}^\star}$ such that the two extracted sequences
nodes.statement_short: A sequence whose types converge to a mixture $\beta P'_A+(1-\beta)P''_A$ splits into two subsequences, in proportion $\beta$, with types converging to $P'_A$ and $P''_A$.
nodes.label: lemma:typesplit

nodes.name: Mixture decomposition of $P_A$
nodes.statement: P_A = \beta P'_A + (1-\beta)P''_A.

nodes.name: Convergence of split types
nodes.statement: & T_{b^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} (\beta, 1-\beta), & & \\ & T_{a'^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} P'_A, & & T_{a''^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} P''_A.

nodes.name: $\eta$ Lipschitz
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz bound via removal of factors and subadditivity of $H_\chi$.

nodes.name: Reduce to chromatic entropies
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 1, bound the normalized difference of chromatic entropies along converging type sequences.

nodes.name: Difference to bound
nodes.statement: \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n}\left|H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n} (a)}\right) - H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}'^n} (a)}\right)\right|
nodes.label: eq:prooflemmaetaconvexA0

nodes.name: Bound the difference
nodes.statement:
Fix $n \in \mathbb{N}^\star$, we assume that the quantity inside $|\cdot|$ in \eqref{eq:prooflemmaetaconvexA0} is positive; the other case can be treated with the same arguments by symmetry of the roles. We have
\begin{align}
    & H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n} (a)}\right) - H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}'^n} (a)}\right) \\
    \leq & \; H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n} (a)}\right) - H_\chi\Bigg(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n \min(T_{\overline{a}^n}(a),T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a))}\! \Bigg) \\
    = & \; H_\chi\Bigg(\!\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n \min(T_{\overline{a}^n}(a),T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a))} \bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n |T_{\overline{a}^n}(a)-T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a)|_+}\!\!\Bigg) \nonumber\\
    & - H_\chi\Bigg(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n \min(T_{\overline{a}^n}(a),T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a))} \Bigg) \\
    \leq & \; H_\chi\Bigg(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n |T_{\overline{a}^n}(a)-T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a)|_+}\Bigg) \\
    \leq & \; \log\left(\max_a |\mathcal{V}_a|\right) \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} n |T_{\overline{a}^n}(a)-T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a)|_+ \\
    \leq & \; n \log\left(\max_a |\mathcal{V}_a|\right) \|T_{\overline{a}^n}-T_{\overline{a}'^n}\|_1, \end{align}
where $|\cdot|_+ = \max(\cdot,0)$ and $\|T_{\overline{a}^n}-T_{\overline{a}'^n}\|_1 = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} |T_{\overline{a}^n}(a)-T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a)|$; \eqref{eq:Th3B} follows from the removal of terms in the second product, as $H_\chi(G\wedge G') \geq H_\chi(G)$ for all probabilistic graphs $G,G'$; \eqref{eq:Th3C} is an arrangement of the terms in the first product, as $\min(s,t) + \max(s-t,0) = s$ for all real numbers $s,t$; \eqref{eq:Th3D} comes from the subadditivity of $H_\chi$; \eqref{eq:Th3E} follows from $H_\chi(G_a) \leq \log \max_{a'} |\mathcal{V}_{a'}|$ for all $a \in \mathcal{A}$; \eqref{eq:Th3F} results from $|T_{\overline{a}^n}(a)-T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a)|_+ \leq |T_{\overline{a}^n}(a)-T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a)|$ for all $a\in \mathcal{A}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the difference by $n\log\max_a|\mathcal{V}_a|$ times the $\ell_1$ distance of the types.

nodes.name: Chain bounding the difference
nodes.statement: & H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n} (a)}\right) - H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}'^n} (a)}\right) \\ \leq & \; H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n} (a)}\right) - H_\chi\Bigg(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n \min(T_{\overline{a}^n}(a),T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a))}\! \Bigg) \\ = & \; H_\chi\Bigg(\!\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n \min(T_{\overline{a}^n}(a),T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a))} \bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n |T_{\overline{a}^n}(a)-T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a)|_+}\!\!\Bigg) \nonumber\\ & - H_\chi\Bigg(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n \min(T_{\overline{a}^n}(a),T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a))} \Bigg) \\ \leq & \; H_\chi\Bigg(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n |T_{\overline{a}^n}(a)-T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a)|_+}\Bigg) \\ \leq & \; \log\left(\max_a |\mathcal{V}_a|\right) \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} n |T_{\overline{a}^n}(a)-T_{\overline{a}'^n}(a)|_+ \\ \leq & \; n \log\left(\max_a |\mathcal{V}_a|\right) \|T_{\overline{a}^n}-T_{\overline{a}'^n}\|_1,
nodes.label: eq:Th3A

nodes.name: Normalize and conclude Lipschitz
nodes.statement_short: Normalize and pass to the limit.

nodes.name: Lipschitz bound
nodes.statement: |\eta(P_A)-\eta(P'_A)| & \leq \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \log\left(\max_a |\mathcal{V}_a|\right)\cdot\|T_{\overline{a}^n}-T_{\overline{a}'^n}\|_1 \\ & = \log\left(\max_a |\mathcal{V}_a|\right)\cdot\|P_A - P'_A\|_1.
nodes.label: eq:Th3G

nodes.name: $\eta$ convex
nodes.statement_short: Convexity by splitting the type sequence (Lemma 10) and subadditivity.

nodes.name: Express eta at a mixture
nodes.statement_short: Write $\eta$ at the mixture as a limit via Lemma 1.

nodes.name: Eta at a mixture
nodes.statement: \eta\big(\beta P'_A + (1-\beta) P''_A\big) = \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge n T_{\overline{a}^n} (a)}\right),
nodes.label: eq:Th3H

nodes.name: Split the sequence
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 10 splits the sequence into two subsequences with the required types.

nodes.name: Split type convergences
nodes.statement: & T_{b^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} (\beta,1-\beta), & & \\ & T_{a'^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} P'_A, & & T_{a''^n} \underset{n \rightarrow \infty}{\rightarrow} P''_A.
nodes.label: eq:Th3J

nodes.name: Subadditivity gives convexity
nodes.statement:
For all $n \in \mathbb{N}^\star$, let $\Xi(n) \doteq n T_{b^n}(0)$, we have
\begin{align}
    & \eta\big(\beta P'_A + (1-\beta) P''_A\big) \\
    = & \; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge \Xi(n) T_{a'^{\Xi(n)}}(a) + (n-\Xi(n)) T_{a''^{n-\Xi(n)}}(a) } \right) \\
    \leq & \; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\Xi(n)}{n} \frac{1}{\Xi(n)} H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge \Xi(n) T_{a'^{\Xi(n)}}(a)}\right) \\
    & + \frac{n-\Xi(n)}{n} \frac{1}{n-\Xi(n)}  H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge (n-\Xi(n)) T_{a''^{n-\Xi(n)}}(a)}\right) \\
    = & \; \beta \eta(P'_A) + (1-\beta)\eta(P''_A); \end{align}
where \eqref{eq:Th3L} comes from \eqref{eq:Th3H}; \eqref{eq:Th3M} follows from the subadditivity of $H_\chi$; \eqref{eq:Th3O} comes from \eqref{eq:Th3J}, \eqref{eq:Th3K} and Lemma \ref{lemma:partvalues}. Since \eqref{eq:Th3O} holds for all $P'_A, P''_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$ and $\beta \in (0,1)$, we have that $\eta$ is convex.
nodes.statement_short: Subadditivity of $H_\chi$ splits the AND product and yields $\eta(\beta P'+(1-\beta)P'')\le\beta\eta(P')+(1-\beta)\eta(P'')$.

nodes.name: Convexity chain
nodes.statement: & \eta\big(\beta P'_A + (1-\beta) P''_A\big) \\ = & \; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge \Xi(n) T_{a'^{\Xi(n)}}(a) + (n-\Xi(n)) T_{a''^{n-\Xi(n)}}(a) } \right) \\ \leq & \; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\Xi(n)}{n} \frac{1}{\Xi(n)} H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge \Xi(n) T_{a'^{\Xi(n)}}(a)}\right) \\ & + \frac{n-\Xi(n)}{n} \frac{1}{n-\Xi(n)} H_\chi\left(\bigwedge_{a \in \mathcal{A}} G_a^{\wedge (n-\Xi(n)) T_{a''^{n-\Xi(n)}}(a)}\right) \\ = & \; \beta \eta(P'_A) + (1-\beta)\eta(P''_A);
nodes.label: eq:Th3L

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement_short: Take a supporting linear minorant $m$ touching $\gamma$ at the interior point; full support forces $\gamma=m$ at the vertices, hence everywhere.

nodes.name: Easy direction
nodes.statement_short: The global identity trivially implies the interior-point one.

nodes.name: Two linearity conditions
nodes.statement: & \exists P_A \in \mathrm{int}(\Delta(\mathcal{A})), \, \gamma(P_A) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \gamma(\mathds{1}_a) \\ \Longleftarrow \;\; & \forall P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A}), \, \gamma(P_A) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \gamma(\mathds{1}_a).
nodes.label: eq:prooflemmaconvexanA1

nodes.name: Hard direction
nodes.statement_short: Supporting-hyperplane argument for the nontrivial implication.

nodes.name: Supporting linear minorant
nodes.statement: Let $P^*_A \in \mathrm{int}\Delta(\mathcal{A})$ such that $\gamma(P^*_A) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P^*_A(a) \gamma(\mathds{1}_a)$. Let $m : \Delta(\mathcal{A}) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ linear such that $m(P^*_A) = \gamma(P^*_A)$ and $\forall P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A}),\, m(P_A) \leq \gamma(P_A)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the interior point and a linear minorant $m$ of $\gamma$ touching it there.

nodes.name: Agreement at the vertices
nodes.statement_short: Full support forces $\gamma = m$ at every vertex $\mathds{1}_a$.

nodes.name: Zero gap at the interior point
nodes.statement: 0 = \gamma(P^*_A) - m(P^*_A) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P^*_A(a) \big(\gamma(\mathds{1}_a) - m(\mathds{1}_a)\big);

nodes.name: Conclude linearity
nodes.statement_short: Convexity gives $\gamma\le m$, so $\gamma=m$ is linear.

nodes.name: Upper bound by interpolation
nodes.statement: f(P_A) & \leq \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \gamma(\mathds{1}_a) \\ & = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) m(\mathds{1}_a) = m(P_A),

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement_short: Achievability: build a product-form random independent set $W^*$ independent of the component index; converse: chain rule of mutual information componentwise.

nodes.name: Set up
nodes.statement: Let $G_a = (\mathcal{V}_a, \mathcal{E}_a, P_{V_a})$, and $G = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E},P_{V})$ such that $G = \bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a$. Let $A$ be the random variable with distribution $P_A$ such that $V = V_A$, i.e. $P_{V|A = a} = P_{V_a}$.\newline
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the disjoint union $G$ and the component index $A$.

nodes.name: Achievability
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound $H_\kappa(G)\le\sum_a P_A(a)H_\kappa(G_a)$ via a constructed $W^*$.

nodes.name: Componentwise minimizers
nodes.statement_short: Take an optimal $W^*_a$ for each component.

nodes.name: Componentwise Körner minimization
nodes.statement: \min_{V_a \in W_a \in \Gamma(G_a)} I(V_a;W_a).
nodes.label: eq:defWastar

nodes.name: Construct W*
nodes.statement_short: Define $W^*$ as a product of the componentwise conditional laws.

nodes.name: Definition of $W^*$
nodes.statement: P_{W^*| A = a, V = v_a}(\mathcal{S}) \doteq P_{W^*_a|V_a = v_a}(\mathcal{S}_a) \prod_{\substack{a' \in \mathcal{A} \\ a' \neq a}} P_{W^*_{a'}}(\mathcal{S}_{a'}),
nodes.label: eq:defWstar

nodes.name: W* takes independent-set values
nodes.statement_short: $W^*$ is supported on independent sets of $G$.

nodes.name: Support of $W^*$
nodes.statement: P_{W^*}(\mathcal{S}) > 0 \Longrightarrow \forall a \in \mathcal{A}, \, P_{W^*_a}(\mathcal{S}_a) > 0.

nodes.name: W* independent of A
nodes.statement_short: The law of $W^*$ given $A=a$ does not depend on $a$.

nodes.name: Conditional law of $W^*$
nodes.statement: P_{W^*| A = a}(\mathcal{S}) = & \sum_{v_a \in \mathcal{V}_a} P_{V_a}(v_a) P_{W^*| A = a, V = v_a}(\mathcal{S}) \\ = & \sum_{v_a \in \mathcal{V}_a} P_{V_a}(v_a) P_{W^*_a|V_a = v_a}(\mathcal{S}_a) \prod_{\substack{a' \in \mathcal{A} \\ a' \neq a}} P_{W^*_{a'}}(\mathcal{S}_{a'}) \\ = & \prod_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} P_{W^*_{a'}}(\mathcal{S}_{a'}).
nodes.label: eq:proofHkappasplitW2

nodes.name: W* is a distribution
nodes.statement_short: $P_{W^*}$ sums to one.

nodes.name: Normalization of $P_{W^*}$
nodes.statement: \sum_{\mathcal{S} \in \Gamma(G)} P_{W^*}(\mathcal{S}) = & \; \sum_{\mathcal{S} \in \Gamma(G)} \;\;\prod_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} P_{W^*_{a'}}(\mathcal{S}_{a'}) \\ = & \; \sum_{(\mathcal{S}_{a'})_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} \in \prod_{a' \in \mathcal{A}} \Gamma(G_{a'})} \;\; \prod_{a' \in \mathcal{A}}P_{W^*_{a'}}(\mathcal{S}_{a'}) \\ = & \; 1,
nodes.label: eq:proofHkappasplitX2

nodes.name: V in W* almost surely
nodes.statement_short: Every set in the support of $W^*$ given $V=v_a$ contains $v_a$.

nodes.name: Supports
nodes.statement_short: Supports of $W^*$ restricted to $\mathcal{V}_a$ are those of $W^*_a$.

nodes.name: Support identity
nodes.statement: \lbrace \mathcal{S} \cap \mathcal{V}_a \:|\: \mathcal{S} \in \mathrm{supp} P_{W^*|V = v_a} \rbrace = \mathrm{supp} P_{W^*_a|V_a = v_a};

nodes.name: Contain the vertex
nodes.statement: Since $V_a \in W^*_a$ with probability one, all the sets in $\mathrm{supp} P_{W^*_a|V_a = v_a}$ contain $v_a$, hence all sets in $\mathrm{supp} P_{W^*|V = v_a}$ also contain $v_a$: $V \in W^*$ with probability one.
nodes.statement_short: Hence the sets contain the vertex.

nodes.name: Combine into the upper bound
nodes.statement:
Now let us combine the results on $W^*$:
\begin{align}
    H_\kappa(G) & \leq I(V;W^*) \\
    & = I(V,A;W^*) \\
    & = I(A;W^*) + \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) I(V;W^*|A = a) \\
    & = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) I(V_a;W_a^*) \\
    & = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) H_\kappa(G_a); \end{align}
where \eqref{eq:proofHkappasplitZ1} holds as $W^*$ takes its values in $\Gamma(G)$ and $V \in W^*$ with probability one; \eqref{eq:proofHkappasplitZ2} holds as $A$ is a deterministic function of $V$; \eqref{eq:proofHkappasplitZ3} comes from the decomposition $I(V,A;W) = I(V;W|A) + I(A;W)$; \eqref{eq:proofHkappasplitZ4} follows from the independence of $A$ and $W^*$; \eqref{eq:proofHkappasplitZ5} comes from the fact that $W^*_a$ minimizes \eqref{eq:defWastar}. \newline
nodes.statement_short: Mutual-information chain gives the upper bound.

nodes.name: Achievability chain
nodes.statement: H_\kappa(G) & \leq I(V;W^*) \\ & = I(V,A;W^*) \\ & = I(A;W^*) + \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) I(V;W^*|A = a)\\ & = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) I(V_a;W_a^*) \\ & = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) H_\kappa(G_a);
nodes.label: eq:proofHkappasplitZ1

nodes.name: Converse
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound by decomposing $I(V,A;W)$ and minimizing componentwise.

nodes.name: Converse chain
nodes.statement: \!\!H_\kappa\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \right) & = \min_{V \in W \in \Gamma(G)} I(V,A;W) \\ & \geq \min_{V \in W \in \Gamma(G)} \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) I(V;W|A = a) \\ & = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \min_{V \in W \in \Gamma(G)} \! I(V;W|A = a) \\ & = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) \min_{V_a \in W \in \Gamma(G_a)} I(V_a;W) \\ & = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} P_A(a) H_\kappa(G_a);
nodes.label: eq:proofHkappasplitA2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement:
$(\Longrightarrow)$ Let $G = \bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a$ be a perfect probabilistic graph. Let $a' \in \mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{S}_{a'} \subset \mathcal{V}_{a'}$. We have $\chi\big(\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \big)[\mathcal{S}_{a'}]\big) = \omega\big(\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \big)[\mathcal{S}_{a'}]\big)$ since $G$ is perfect, and therefore $\chi(G_{a'}[\mathcal{S}_{a'}]) = \omega(G_{a'}[\mathcal{S}_{a'}])$, as $\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \big)[\mathcal{S}_{a'}] = G_{a'}[\mathcal{S}_{a'}]$. Thus all the graphs $(G_a)_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ are perfect.

$(\Longleftarrow)$ Conversely, assume that for all $a \in \mathcal{A}$, $G_a = (\mathcal{V}_a, \mathcal{E}_a, P_{V_a})$ is perfect. Then for all $\mathcal{S} \subset \bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \mathcal{V}_a$, $\mathcal{S}$ can be written as $\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \mathcal{S}_a$ where $\mathcal{S}_a \subset \mathcal{V}_a$ for all $a \in \mathcal{A}$, and we have for all $P_A \in \Delta(\mathcal{A})$:
\begin{align}
    \chi\left(\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a \right)[\mathcal{S}]\right) & = \chi\left(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a[\mathcal{S}_a] \right) \\
    & = \max_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \chi\left(G_a[\mathcal{S}_a]\right) \\
    & = \max_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \omega\left(G_a[\mathcal{S}_a]\right), \end{align}
and similarly, $\omega\big(\big(\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a\big)[\mathcal{S}]\big) = \max_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \omega\left(G_a[\mathcal{S}_a]\right)$.
Hence $\bigsqcup_{a \in \mathcal{A}}^{P_A} G_a$ is also perfect.
nodes.statement_short: Induced subgraphs of the disjoint union inside one component are induced subgraphs of that component; conversely $\chi$ and $\omega$ of a disjoint union are maxima over components.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9
nodes.statement:
Let $c^* : \mathcal{V} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}$ and $c^*_\mathcal{S} : \mathcal{S} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}$ be the optimal colorings of $G$ and $G[\mathcal{S}]$, respectively. Consider the coloring $c : \mathcal{V} \rightarrow \mathcal{C} \sqcup \mathcal{V}$ of $G$ defined by $c(v) = c^*_\mathcal{S}$ if $v \in \mathcal{S}$, $c(v) = v$ otherwise.\newline

\textbf{(Lower bound)} On one hand, we have
\begin{align}
    H_\chi(G) \leq &\: H(c(V), \mathds{1}_{V \in \mathcal{S}}) \\
    = &\: H(\mathds{1}_{V \in \mathcal{S}}) + P_V(\mathcal{S}) H(c(V)|V \in \mathcal{S}) \nonumber\\
     &+ (1-P_V(\mathcal{S})) H(c(V)|V \notin \mathcal{S}) \\
    \leq &\: 1 + H(c^*_\mathcal{S}(V)|V \in \mathcal{S}) + (1-P_V(\mathcal{S})) \log |\mathcal{V}| \\
    = &\: H_\chi(G[\mathcal{S}]) + 1 + (1-P_V(\mathcal{S})) \log |\mathcal{V}|; \end{align}
where \eqref{eq:prooflemmainducedA1} comes from the fact that $c$ is a coloring of $G$; \eqref{eq:prooflemmainducedA2} is a decomposition using conditional entropies; \eqref{eq:prooflemmainducedA3} comes from the construction of $c$: $c|_\mathcal{S} = c^*_{\mathcal{S}}$; \eqref{eq:prooflemmainducedA4} follows from the optimality of $c^*_\mathcal{S}$ as a coloring of $G[\mathcal{S}]$.\newline

\textbf{(Upper bound)} On the other hand, 
\begin{align}
    & H_\chi(G[\mathcal{S}]) \nonumber\\
    \leq & \: H(c^*(V) | V \in \mathcal{S}) \\
    = & \, \frac{1}{P_V(\mathcal{S})}\Big(\!H(c^*(V)| \mathds{1}_{V \in \mathcal{S}}) - (1-P_V(\mathcal{S}))H(c^*(V) | V \notin \mathcal{S})\!\Big) \\
    \leq & \: \frac{H(c^*(V))}{P_V(\mathcal{S})} = \frac{H_\chi(G)}{P_V(\mathcal{S})} \end{align}
where \eqref{eq:prooflemmainducedB1} comes from the fact that $c^*$ induces a coloring of $G[\mathcal{S}]$; \eqref{eq:prooflemmainducedB2} is a decomposition using conditional entropies; \eqref{eq:prooflemmainducedB3} results from the elimination of negative terms and the optimality of $c^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound by extending an optimal coloring of $G[\mathcal{S}]$ with fresh colors outside $\mathcal{S}$; upper bound by restricting an optimal coloring of $G$.
